extracted.intended_audience: industry partners, innovators, biotech/diagnostics companies, academic developers, and other organizations seeking BARDA partnership or funding for medical countermeasures
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of BARDA's mission, program divisions, and funding/partnership mechanisms for developing medical countermeasures (MCMs), including solicitation vehicles (BAA, EZ-BAA), program focus areas (CBRN, vaccines, diagnostics, etc.), and criteria implicit in BARDA's support (e.g., readiness, regulatory/compliance, manufacturing scale-up, sustainability).

rubrics_metrics.name: BARDA Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Areas of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: BARDA’s Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) sets forth the advanced research and development Areas of Interest (AOIs) and solicits proposals focusing on these areas in order to protect the United States against public health emergency threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the BAA to submit proposals aligned to BARDA AOIs; proposals should target BARDA-defined threat areas and advanced R&D priorities. (Page text provides the mechanism but not scoring details.)

rubrics_metrics.name: BARDA Easy Broad Agency Announcement (EZ-BAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: To spur innovation, BARDA has issued its business-friendly, streamlined Easy Broad Agency Announcement (EZ-BAA) to support a number of new medical countermeasures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EZ-BAA is intended as a streamlined, business-friendly solicitation vehicle—suitable for innovators seeking faster or lower-burden entry points to BARDA funding. (No formal scoring guidance on page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Request TechWatch Meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are interested in partnering with the federal government on medical countermeasures, submit your ideas to a platform that reaches a host of potential federal partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement via TechWatch is an avenue to present ideas and obtain feedback/visibility to federal partners; useful for preliminary alignment before formal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Product Profiles (TPP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Target Product Profiles (TPP) (listed as a program link on the site).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPPs are BARDA-referenced tools that define desired product attributes and regulatory/end-user expectations; developers should align product specifications and development plans to relevant TPPs. (The page only lists the TPP resource without detailed content.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) (listed as a program link on the site).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BARDA uses TRLs to characterize maturity; proposals should state current TRL and a plan to advance readiness. (Page lists TRLs but does not provide the TRL scale text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: CBRN Division program focus: end-to-end development to FDA approval
rubrics_metrics.description: CBRN helps innovators develop promising MCMs from preclinical development to clinical trials and manufacturing scale-up to FDA approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BARDA values candidates with a credible pathway from preclinical through clinical development and manufacturing scale-up toward FDA approval; proposals should address each phase and the plan to reach regulatory milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: DRIVe: accelerate transformative technologies and de-risking
rubrics_metrics.description: DRIVe works to accelerate the development and availability of transformative technologies and approaches to protect Americans from health security threats. DRIVe aims to de-risk the most promising technologies and capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals to DRIVe should focus on transformative, high-impact innovations and include strategies for de-risking and moving toward commercialization; emphasis on novel approaches and ecosystem-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: DNCD/nonclinical development expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: DNCD provides nonclinical models, tools, and expertise to advance MCM development. DNCD provides expertise and laboratory capacity to establish and share nonclinical models, conduct appropriate nonclinical studies to support FDA approval, and evaluate potential MCM candidates prior to BARDA investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong nonclinical data and appropriate models are expected to advance toward BARDA investment; developers should plan and document nonclinical studies that will support regulatory filings and candidate evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Development (DCD) support criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing expert knowledge and support to BARDA’s programs in advanced product development and clinical research, including supporting BARDA clinical studies via the Clinical Studies Network (CSN). Integrated centralized resource: Our focus is BARDA’s success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical readiness and high-quality clinical development plans, including capability to participate in BARDA-supported clinical networks, are key evaluative elements for clinical-stage proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract Management and Acquisition (CMA) procurement flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: CMA provides flexible and innovative acquisition solutions in support of BARDA’s mission. CMA strives to enhance the U.S. government’s contracting capabilities to respond quickly to both known and emerging public health threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BARDA acquisition considers flexible contracting approaches; proposers should be prepared to engage with government contracting mechanisms and may benefit from proposing procurement-ready solutions or scalable contracting options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection, Diagnostics, and Devices Infrastructure (DDDI) investments
rubrics_metrics.description: DDDI invests in diagnostics and devices across the spectrum of advanced research and development, stockpiling, and domestic manufacturing capacity expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals in diagnostics/devices should address R&D, suitability for stockpiling, and plans to expand or secure domestic manufacturing capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmaceutical Countermeasures & Infrastructure (PCI) manufacturing/resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI provides expertise to strengthen the nation’s ability to manufacture, distribute, administer, and scale production of lifesaving MCMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that strengthen manufacturing, distribution, administration, and scalability (including public–private partnerships and manufacturing readiness) align with PCI priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory & Quality Affairs (RQA) compliance and regulatory readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: RQA ensures that BARDA-supported MCMs are safe, effective, and in compliance with relevant and current laws, regulations, and guidelines by providing technical expertise and innovative regulatory and policy approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory strategy, quality systems, and compliance with applicable regulations are essential; proposals should include regulatory pathways and quality management plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influenza & Emerging Infectious Diseases (IEID) priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Influenza & EID invests in advanced research and development, manufacturing capacity, and procurement of MCMs to protect the nation from pandemic influenza and other emerging infectious diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions targeting pandemic influenza or emerging infectious diseases should demonstrate relevance to pandemic preparedness, manufacturing surge capacity, and procurement-readiness (e.g., pre-pandemic vaccine stockpile needs such as NPIVS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonclinical/clinical/regulatory integration across divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective BARDA divisions and subject-matter experts support the advanced development of life-saving drugs, vaccines, therapeutics, diagnostics, and medical devices through collaborations with industry partners and colleagues across the U.S. government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BARDA evaluates proposals for integrated plans across nonclinical, clinical, manufacturing, and regulatory domains and for evidence of effective collaboration with government and industry partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability of portfolio investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient resources are needed for BARDA to maintain and support portfolio investments to ensure long-term access to licensed medical countermeasures (MCMs) that are vital to the nation's health security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BARDA favors strategies that demonstrate long-term sustainability and access (e.g., lifecycle funding plans, maintenance of supply chains, and plans that ensure continued availability of licensed MCMs).

rubrics_metrics.name: BARDA Responds: agility and response posture
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthening BARDA's agile preparedness and response posture to combat health security threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that increase BARDA’s and the nation’s agility to respond to public health emergencies—through rapid development, manufacturing surge, or flexible deployment—align with BARDA Responds priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Initiatives and smaller innovation projects
rubrics_metrics.description: BARDA invests in innovative projects across our portfolio, including promising technologies, platforms, and programs. We launch and support efforts designed to accelerate and foster smaller new projects. (Examples: Project NextGen, REMM, PRISM, CHEMM.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller-scale or high-risk/high-reward projects that can be accelerated or piloted via special initiatives may be appropriate for targeted funding mechanisms; emphasize catalytic impact and rapid learnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of demonstrated regulatory outcomes and prior authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Site references BARDA-supported partners having achieved FDA clearances, approvals, and EUAs (e.g., 'BARDA funded partners have received 32 FDA clearances or approvals and 41 EUAs for countermeasures developed under his leadership').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior demonstration of regulatory progress or clear pathways to authorization (EUA/clearance/approval) is a favorable signal; proposals should document regulatory milestones and historical performance where available.
